note: Both sets share the same core readings of Figures 2-10, including several conflicting near-duplicate values (mass density 3,100 vs 3,000 kg/m at r/R=0, axial 4.5e10 vs 4.7e10 N at r/R=0, torsional 0.9e11 vs 1.0e11 N·m^2 at r/R=0, and 0 vs 100 kg/m at the tip). Set A's two extra claims on Figure 2-11 are both wrong: 2 m at the root is the blade planform edge, not the geometric center (near 0.3 m), and −4 m is the axis minimum, not the shear center at r/R=0.2 (near 0.1 m). Set B's extras are better — torsional ≈0.8e11 N·m^2 at the root matches the curve — though its flap 1.2e11 N·m^2 at the root misreads a y-axis tick (the curve starts near 1.5e11) and it repeats the axial tip claim. On balance B makes fewer wrong claims, so it is the better set.
remarks: Both sets quote only concatenated axis labels, legend entries and tick numbers, so no quote actually supports the numeric value claimed (e.g. 'Mass density [kg/m] ... Nondimensional Blade Span (r/R)' cannot support 3100 kg/m). Both sets also emit several claims for the same point with conflicting values (root mass density, root torsional stiffness, root axial stiffness, tip mass density), which looks like curve points and axis ticks being sampled indiscriminately. Neither set captures the mass center, neutral center or pitch axis chordwise curves of Figure 2-11, and the correct geometric/shear center values are absent from both. All plotted values are read visually from the figure and are approximate to about ±0.1 of each axis division.
